review: S5 HRTB FnMut output opt-in semantic review
scope: Static review of the final R16 actual-body runner/profile route and existing R13 translator HRTB projection path. No compiler, Cloud build, raw evidence, or proof-credit claims were used.
basis: The profile body pin matches the reviewed R16 body bytes and enables HRTB output only alongside the exact full-body c1 recovery and deferred-scope route. The runner adds metadata only after checking those conditions and the exact sort4_stable body name.

run_case requires c1 recovery, scope relocation, and sort4_stable before setting SORT4_HRTB_OUTPUT=1 and SORT4_HRTB_OUTPUT_TARGETS=sort4_stable. It removes both variables for other bodies, and the dedicated hrtb-opt-in-off control removes both while retaining c1 and scope opt-ins. Service tests cover this routing, ambient-variable isolation, and refusal when route prerequisites are absent; parent reports 39 tests passing (8 registration, 31 service).

Translator target parsing is fail-closed for malformed/duplicate targets. HRTB bounds are extracted only from compiler-origin clauses matching FnOnce::Output over two distinct bound regions and the matching FnMut trait clause, with the same type parameter in both references and Bool output. Emission further requires the exact compiler FnMut::call_mut source and translated item, two call arguments, matching source substitutions/type arguments, one shared call-site lifetime, and exactly one matching extracted (F,T) bound.

The emitted projection equality is a verifier assertion through #register_type_projection_equality; it does not introduce an assumed lemma or alter the kernel. Existing actual-source, strict-scope, c1, deferred-scope, referent-address, and exact-body guards remain prerequisites. The opt-in is isolated from diagnostic/native routes, whose environment guards reject this HRTB setting.
limits: This is a semantic source/wiring review, not execution evidence. The final HRTB-enabled Cloud preflight remains necessary to check compiled integration and report the exact body/control statuses.
No source-reported failure or negative-control observation establishes proof success. Independent proof credit remains zero until the authorized Brief establishes it.
